_doc: Reactive rules of barch-events (agent/events.py): when an event happens or a metric crosses a line, do something.
Rule: id, description, when, do (shell commands, run in order; {field} placeholders are shell-quoted), notify (text of a
notification; title is the description), say (spoken through barch voice), ask (notify with a Run button instead of acting),
cooldown (30s 5m 2h 1d; default 60s), critical (notification urgency), enabled (default true).
when: {event: name, <field>: regex...} matches an event by name and regexes on its fields (search, case-insensitive);
{metric: name, above|below: value, clear: value} fires once when the metric crosses the line and re-arms past clear.
Events: window.open/close/urgent (address, class, title, workspace), window.fullscreen (on), monitor.added/removed (name,

description), vpn.up (region, name, country), vpn.down (it dropped) / vpn.off (turned off: Disconnect, Anonymous Mode off, voice), both with the tunnel that went away (region, name, country) plus killswitch (armed|off) and note, anon.on/off, net.up/down (dev), pods.connected/disconnected (name),

session.locked/unlocked, failure (unit, path), boot (seconds, text, kernel), claude.cost (source, usd, note), startup (boot_age_s), music.review (an album of the NAS music pipeline waits in the review queue: id, name, folder, problem, problems, cover_only yes|no), video.foreign (a movie or episode file of the video pipeline has audio beyond the original language and PT-BR: id, kind, title, file, original, audio, extra, por yes|no, trim pending|waiting|failed|skipped|none, text; every video_every_s).

NAS (agent/nas.py, Unraid's API, `barch nas status`; every nas_every_s, certificates every nas_certs_every_s): nas.down (error) after three misses, nas.up, nas.array (state, previous), nas.disk (names, count, text), nas.containers (down for longer than nas_grace_s: names, count, text), nas.alert (Unraid's unread notifications: importance ALERT|WARNING, count, text), cert.expiring (under cert_warn_days, again under 3, or refused: hosts, count, days, text).

Firewalls (agent/pfsense.py, the pfSense REST API of each site in ~/.config/barch/pfsense.json, `barch fw status`; every fw_every_s): fw.down (site, error, text) after three misses, fw.up, fw.auth (the key was refused; left alone for fw_auth_backoff_s), fw.boot (uptime), fw.gateway (name, status, ok yes|no), fw.interface (name, status, up), fw.ipsec (name, up), fw.dnsbl (ok: the DNSBL stopped answering its virtual IP for a blocked domain), fw.client (a MAC never seen on that site took a lease: mac, ip, hostname, if, online); every one carries site and text.
Metrics: cpu.temp cpu.pct cpu.load1 temp.<hwmon> gpu.temp gpu.util gpu.power gpu.vram_pct ram.pct swap.pct disk.<root|home>.pct

disk.<..>.free_gb net.latency_ms vpn.latency_ms vpn.connected pods.<left|right|case>.pct health.issues health.failed_units boot.seconds nas.up nas.cpu.pct nas.ram.pct nas.array.pct nas.pool.pct (the fullest pool) nas.disk.temp (the hottest) nas.disks.bad nas.containers.down nas.containers.updates nas.alerts cert.days (the certificate closest to expiring) fw.<site>.up fw.<site>.cpu.pct fw.<site>.ram.pct fw.<site>.temp fw.<site>.clients fw.<site>.ipsec.up fw.<site>.dnsbl fw.<site>.gw.<gateway>.rtt|loss fw.<site>.blocked (connections the firewall blocked since the last sample) fw.<site>.blocked.<interface>.
`barch rules list|test|fire|enable|disable`, `barch events log`, `barch metrics list|series|summary`; the daemon reloads this file by itself.
